title: Wi-Fi setup mode
causes: The fridge is acting as a Wi-Fi access point for SmartThings setup.
steps: Finish the setup in the SmartThings app, or wait. The code clears by itself.
technician: This is not a fault. No service is needed.

title: Freezer fan error
causes: The freezer fan is frozen in ice, often after a door was left open or a gasket did not seal.
The fan motor has failed.
steps: Check that the freezer door closes and the gasket seals all round.
Do not overpack the freezer.
If you can, move food out and let the fridge defrost with the doors open.
technician: If the code returns after defrosting, the fan needs a Samsung technician.

title: Fridge fan error
causes: The fridge door was left open too long and the fan iced up.
steps: Move food to a cool place.
Unplug the fridge and leave the doors open for a few hours.
Plug it back in and close the doors.
technician: If 22E comes back, request Samsung service.

title: Family Hub fault
causes: A software issue on the Family Hub screen.
steps: Install the latest software update.
Tap OK the first time the code appears after updating.
technician: If it keeps returning after the update, request Samsung service.

title: Water in AutoFill compartment
causes: The AutoFill water pitcher is leaking into its compartment.
steps: Remove the pitcher and dry the compartment.
Check the pitcher is seated correctly and not cracked.
technician: If water keeps collecting, contact Samsung service.

title: Low supply voltage (Family Hub)
causes: Usually a short power cut.
steps: Press and hold OK for 3 seconds to clear it.
technician: Harmless on its own. Contact Samsung only if it appears often.

title: Communication fault at start-up
causes: Power was disrupted while the fridge was starting up.
steps: Unplug the fridge or switch off its breaker for 60 seconds.
Restore power and check whether the code comes back.
technician: If the code returns after a reset, request Samsung service.

title: Compressor abnormal current
causes: A power surge or electrical problem.
steps: Unplug the fridge or switch off its breaker for 60 seconds.
Restore power and check whether the code comes back.
technician: If 83E returns, request Samsung service.

title: Compressor low voltage
causes: A brown-out or low mains voltage.
steps: Unplug the fridge or switch off its breaker for 60 seconds.
Restore power and check whether the code comes back.
technician: If 85E returns, have the supply checked and request Samsung service.

title: Compressor high voltage
causes: A power surge, for example during a storm.
steps: Unplug the fridge or switch off its breaker for 60 seconds.
Restore power and check whether the code comes back.
technician: If 86E returns, request Samsung service.

title: Internal communication error
causes: A recent power surge.
The door wiring connector is not connected properly.
steps: Switch off power at the plug or breaker.
Check and reconnect the wiring connector above the door hinge.
Restore power.
technician: If the code returns, request Samsung service.

title: Cooling Off (demo) mode
causes: Demo or shop mode is switched on, often by accident. The fridge does not cool.
steps: Press and hold the top two buttons on the left of the panel for 5 to 8 seconds until it chimes.
On some models, also hold the top right button.
Check your manual for your model's button combination.
technician: No service needed. This is a setting, not a fault.

title: Fridge defrost sensor error
causes: The fridge defrost sensor is faulty.
steps: Do not unplug the fridge unless told to.
Keep the doors closed as much as possible to protect the food.
technician: Request Samsung service to replace or check the sensor.

title: Ice maker sensor error (freezer)
causes: The ice maker sensor in the freezer is faulty.
steps: Switch off the ice maker if you can.
Keep using the fridge as normal.
technician: Request Samsung service.

title: Ice pipe heater error

title: Ice maker function error

technician: If the code stays, request Samsung service.

Set the freezer to -18 °C.
Keep food away from the air vents.
Check the door seals by closing the door on a sheet of paper. It should not slide out easily.
Open the doors less often.
technician: If the freezer still does not cool, request LG service.

The water container is not seated or its float is stuck.
A software fault.
steps: Straighten any kink in the water hose.
Clean the inlet filter.
Remove the water container, clean under it and push it fully back in.
Shake the container to check the float moves freely.
Set the freezer to -18 °C for at least 48 hours.
technician: If the fault stays, contact Miele Customer Service.

title: Software crash

steps: Unplug the appliance for about 2 minutes.
Plug it back in and switch it on.
If it works again, restore factory settings from the Settings menu.
technician: If the fault returns, contact Miele Customer Service.

Do not refreeze thawed food unless you cook it first.
technician: Not a fault. Contact Miele only if it appears without any power cut.

Keep the doors closed until the code clears.
Use or cook any thawed food soon.
Do not add fresh food until the code has gone.
technician: If the code stays on, contact an authorised AEG technician.

title: Fridge not cold enough

technician: If E10 persists, book an AEG repair.
